title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Sanjay Patel
release_notes: Tuned continuous batcher scheduler to reduce starvation and improve fairness under mixed priority workloads; added configurable per-route max-queue-timeouts and backpressure signals; default behavior preserves legacy latency SLOs while improving throughput utilization.
description: Motivation: The continuous batcher scheduler has historically prioritized throughput but under mixed-priority traffic patterns we observed starvation of lower-priority routes and unbounded queue growth under transient load spikes. This caused customer-facing latency tails and instances where KV cache reuse fell dramatically because requests were delayed beyond cache TTLs. This PR tunes queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeout behavior to balance latency SLOs and utilization. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a weighted fair queueing layer for the continuous batcher scheduler that assigns tokens to route classes based on configurable weights; 2) Add a soft starvation detector that temporarily boosts scheduling weight for routes that have been queued longer than starve_threshold_ms; 3) Enforce per-request max_queue_time_ms with a graceful backpressure response instead of unbounded queueing; 4) Add per-route and global backpressure signals to upstream router and API gateway to enable early rejection/redirect to fallback model variants; 5) Improve scheduler telemetry: per-queue wait histograms, starved-route counters, and timeout rejection metrics; 6) Optimize wakeup/kicker paths to reduce contention on hot GPU worker queues, including a micro-optimization in the kernel selection hotpath to avoid an atomic when waiting_count==0. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime config continuous_batcher.v2.enabled=false by default, gradual rollout to 10% of traffic in internal canary, expanded to 50% after 24h if no regression in latency P95 or error rate, full rollout after 72h and manual signoff. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves legacy scheduling weights and timeout defaults unless the config is enabled. Testing: unit tests for weighted queueing and starvation heuristics, end-to-end load tests in perf-canary harness showing 8-12% throughput improvement and 20-40ms reduction in tail latency for mixed-priority traffic; regression tests added to verify KV cache hit-rate does not regress under the new scheduler. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated and linked - [x] benchmarks added to perf-canary - [x] observability metrics added - [x] integrated with router backpressure signal - [x] rollout config + feature flag - [x] docs/console notes for new per-route configs - [x] security review N/A - [x] manual smoke verification performed in staging Known limitations: We still rely on conservative default weights; extreme priority imbalances may require manual tuning per-tenant. Related: ENG-4829 design, ENG-4890 perf investigations, incident SUP-2187 (hotfix during outage).

Sanjay Patel (2026-02-13): The detector uses exponential backoff for boosts and a cooldown window; added comments and a unit test demonstrating stability under synthetic oscillation patterns.

Sanjay Patel (2026-02-18): Added per-tenant labels to starved_route counter and verified low-cardinality tagging in staging metrics pipeline.

ci_flakiness_notes: One integration test flaky on initial run (integration_test.go: TestQueueStarvation) due to a race in the test harness; fixed the harness by adding deterministic clock control. All CI checks passing on final run.
benchmarks_summary: Perf-canary mixed-priority workload: 8-12% throughput increase at equivalent P95 latency; tail latency improvements of 20-40ms in heavy skew scenarios; KV cache hit rate improved by 3-6% due to reduced queue-induced cache misses.
files_snippets: runtime/continuous_batcher/queueing/wfq.go: added weighted queueing algorithm with O(1) enqueue/dequeue semantics and weight decay to avoid long-term dominance
runtime/continuous_batcher/queueing/starvation_detector.go: detector monitors per-route queue age percentiles and applies temporary weight boosts with exponential cooldown
runtime/kernel/kernel_selection_hotpath.go: remove atomic increment on fast-path when waiting_count==0 and add comment explaining safe non-atomic path
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge after approvals and green CI; merge commit recreated in main with changelog entry.
changelog_entry: scheduler(continuous-batcher): tune queueing and fairness, add starvation prevention and queue timeouts; telemetry and config added (ENG-4829)
manual_verification: Staging smoke: sent mixed-priority synthetic traffic for 2h, validated no P99 regressions for high-priority routes and improved P95 for mixed workloads; verified per-route max_queue_time_ms enforced and backpressure signals propagated to router.
notes: This PR is part of a broader effort to unify scheduling across Dedicated and Hosted runtimes. Future work: dynamic weight autotuning, per-tenant profiles, and integration with Redwood Optimize recommendations.
